newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah volatile in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah volatile in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was volatile against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday after renewed rumours of a band widening, dealers said.

They said speculation on a band widening, probably spread by offshore players, swept the market late in the afternoon, sending spot dollars down to a low of 2,387.0 from an early high of 2,392.0 before it settled at 2,388.0/88.5 at 0900 GMT.
"I think some banks were hit on large customer orders which forced them to square in the interbank market, driving other players to follow," the dealer said.
Another dealer with a local bank said the rumours came from Singapore as the market had been pretty quiet lately.
"The fall was a bit drastic because long dollar holders were forced to cut losses immediately," he said.
The U.S. bank dealer said some selling interest from London operators remained although the market had settled down.
He said some players seemed to factor in tight rupiah on Friday which might bring the dollar down as well on Wednesday.
Dealers said counter dollar buying from local players helped limit the downside for the dollar.
The rupiah strengthened against the dollar each time the central bank widened its band in the past, causing players to unload dollars quickly each time the rumours emerged.
Swap premiums remained stable in the afternoon. Overnight swaps were at par/0.1 and tom/next at 0.10/0.15 points.
Overnight rupiah was last given at four percent.
One-month swaps were at 9.75/10.75, two at 24.00/25.00, three at 36.00/37.00 and six at 74.50/76.00 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,381/2,573 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,381/2,429 on Tuesday, the first time this week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by three points the previous week.
